1999-01-06: Reports allege that United Nations weapons inspectors passed secret intelligence to the United States, a development that Saddam Hussein was reportedly delighted by and that intensified longstanding suspicions about Unscom.
1999-01-11: Kuwait placed some military units on maximum alert and the US bombed a missile site in northern Iraq after Washington warned Saddam Hussein not to threaten his neighbors.
1999-01-14: Saddam Hussein escalated confrontation with the United States and its Arab allies by issuing new threats to Kuwait, including questioning Kuwait's borders and laying claim to its land and coasts.

2000-11-25: Iraq's Deputy Prime Minister Tariq Aziz arrived in Damascus aboard the first direct Iraqi flight to Syria in nearly two decades, a challenge to UN sanctions that followed the gradual rehabilitation of Iraq among Arab neighbours, in particular in light of Saddam Hussein's outspoken support of the present Palestinian intifada.
2001-01-17: Saddam Hussein marked the tenth anniversary of the Gulf war with a victory speech, while his son Uday called for a map to be redrawn to include Kuwait as part of "greater Iraq".
2001-01-30: Iraq was the first item on the agenda of the US National Security Council at its first meeting, as revealed by Paul O'Neill.
2001-02-18: Saddam Hussein appeared to have won the public relations battle in the Middle East following US-British air strikes on radar stations around Baghdad.
2001-02-19: US and British airstrikes on Iraq fail to secure the return of UN weapons inspectors, as part of efforts to pressure Saddam Hussein's government into compliance.
2001-03-06: Margaret Thatcher, at the 10th anniversary of Kuwait's liberation, laments that Britain and the US failed to wipe out Saddam Hussein at the end of the Gulf war, remarks that leave John Major seething.
2001-04-26: The attorney general asks Scotland Yard to investigate specific cases of British subjects taken hostage on Saddam Hussein's orders in Kuwait and Iraq in 1990.

2001-05-18: Britain's Foreign Office leads UN moves to lift most sanctions on Iraq while aiming to refocus attention on Saddam Hussein's responsibility for Iraqi deprivation and his efforts to acquire weapons of mass destruction.

2001-09-20: President George W. Bush first asked Tony Blair to support the removal of Saddam Hussein from power at a private White House dinner nine days after the September 11 terror attacks.

2002-09-27: Russia expresses skepticism over claims that Saddam Hussein possesses weapons of mass destruction, rejecting British and US diplomatic overtures for a UN resolution threatening Iraq with military action.
2002-09-30: Iraqi generals sent by Saddam Hussein held talks with UN officials in Vienna on practical arrangements for resuming weapons inspections in Iraq.
2002-10-15: Saddam Hussein faces no challenger in Iraq's presidential referendum, seeking another seven-year term as the government pushes for a high "yes" vote.
2002-10-16: Iraqi officials announced that Saddam Hussein secured 100% of the vote in a referendum, awarding him another seven-year term.
2002-10-24: Iran says it would accept US-led military action against Saddam Hussein if UN efforts for a peaceful solution failed, while refusing to take part in a war.

2003-01-10: The Triumph Leader Museum in Baghdad, displaying thousands of state gifts presented to Saddam Hussein since 1979, is described in a news report.
2003-02-04: An Iraqi exile recounts that Saddam Hussein took power in 1979 and describes his rule as a reign of fear, arguing that removing him is a necessity.

2003-02-18: Tony Blair refuses to specify what sort of regime might follow Saddam Hussein's in Iraq despite making the moral case for overthrowing the Iraqi dictator by military action.

2003-03-05: The UK government’s Export Credits Guarantee Department paid around £300,000 to Uhde Ltd after trade debts linked to a chlorine plant contract for Saddam Hussein’s Iraq were written down following the Gulf war.
2003-03-16: Saddam Hussein's Iraq is described as being at the heart of a volatile Middle East, with past actions including the 1980 war against Iran and the 1990 invasion of Kuwait that triggered the first Gulf War and UN disarmament demands leading to the current crisis.

2003-03-24: Saddam Hussein pledged victory over the "enemies of God" in an address broadcast on Iraqi state television, urging Iraqis to "hit the enemies hard" as US and British forces advanced toward Baghdad.

2003-03-28: Anti-war protesters in Tehran denounced both "Bush's barbarism" and "Saddam Hussein's dictatorship" while demonstrating at the British embassy.

2003-04-08: Article discusses uncertainty over whether Saddam Hussein possesses chemical weapons and whether he may use them, while noting US forces have not found hard evidence of such weapons at inspected sites.

2003-04-10: US marines came under heavy fire from suspected Republican Guards while attempting to search a Baghdad mosque where Saddam Hussein was suspected to be hiding, and a US marine was reported killed in the battle.

2003-04-18: Abu Dhabi TV broadcasts footage and an audio recording claiming to show Saddam Hussein in Baghdad on April 9, the day the city fell, suggesting he may have survived.
2003-04-20: Saddam Hussein's son-in-law Jamal Mustafa Sultan Abdullah al-Tikriti was captured after surrendering to the Iraqi National Congress in Baghdad, with US officials hoping he could provide information on Saddam's whereabouts.
2003-04-21: American military officials announce the arrest of Mohammed Hamza al-Zubaidi, a former Iraqi prime minister and member of Saddam Hussein's inner circle, in Hillah.
2003-04-24: Tariq Aziz, a loyal spokesman for Saddam Hussein, was captured by US forces.
2003-04-25: George Galloway's lawyers announce he plans legal action over allegations that he was paid substantial sums by Saddam Hussein's regime, claims Galloway denies as "totally untrue."

2003-12-15: Saddam Hussein was captured, an event widely discussed in editorials as a turning point for Iraq.
2003-12-16: Much Arab press commentary focused on the manner of Saddam Hussein's capture, with some criticizing his humiliating surrender and others celebrating it.
